calls.reason: Stanford documents narrowing benchmark gaps, and the model papers show shared reinforcement learning methods. They do not establish that shared models, techniques, and data explain the convergence.
Brownstein supports the proposed threat to state AI laws, but the packet does not fully establish the scope or absence of substitute protections. Covington confirms the moratorium never became law.

Whiteford and George Mason report continuing state oversight despite federal pressure. The packet provides no comparison showing that removing oversight increased lobbying to preserve weak accountability.

The safety research review identifies commercial incentives alongside neglected protections, and Tsoy's model finds mixed incentives. Neither establishes companies' behavior without regulation or who bears the resulting harms.

Stanford reports alternating leadership and a small US lead through March 2026. That supports close competition, but does not settle whether either country will eventually achieve durable superiority.

Covington confirms the moratorium was removed before enactment. CRS supports the absence of comprehensive federal privacy law, but the packet does not establish whether the proposal would have blocked every state privacy law.
